question: How many temples and monasteries are there in Ellora caves?
solution:
The correct answer is __**34**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ellora Caves are a complex of 34 caves located in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra, India.
 
• The caves consist of Buddhist monasteries, Hindu temples, and Jain temples, showcasing the religious harmony of the time.
 
• The construction of these caves took place between the 6th and 10th centuries, during the rule of various dynasties.
 
• The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, renowned for their rock-cut architecture and intricate carvings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ellora Caves**

 
 
• The Ellora Caves are an impressive complex of rock-cut caves representing three different religions: Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism.
 
• The 12 Buddhist caves (Caves 1–12) primarily consist of monasteries and are the earliest structures, dated between 600 and 730 AD.
 
• The 17 Hindu caves (Caves 13–29) were constructed between 600 and 870 AD and include the remarkable Kailasa temple (Cave 16), which is the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world.
 
• The 5 Jain caves (Caves 30–34) were built between 800 and 1000 AD and are known for their detailed carvings and intricate craftsmanship.
 
• Ellora is known for its architectural brilliance, including intricate carvings, sculptures, and frescoes that depict deities, mythical creatures, and scenes from ancient texts.
